title: Provider settings migration writes bare-host base URLs verbatim into providers.json
description:
## Summary

The settings.json → providers.json migration (#14928, not yet released) copies `authentication.<key>.baseUrl` values into `~/.posit/ai/providers.json` verbatim. A bare known-provider host (e.g. `https://api.anthropic.com`, missing the `/v1` segment the AI SDKs require) works in the legacy settings channel but is broken in providers.json — so the migration can turn a working configuration into a failing one.

## Why bare hosts work in settings but not in providers.json

Positron's sign-in dialog historically prefilled bare API hosts into `authentication.*.baseUrl` (#14775). The fix corrects them at the read seam (`normalizeBaseUrlForProvider`), so a bare host in settings behaves correctly today. providers.json has no such correction by design — the provider bridge trusts `baseUrl` as given, and the SDK appends only the operation path: `POST https://api.anthropic.com/messages` → 404, while `…/v1/messages` reaches the API.

The migration bridges the value from the channel where it's corrected into the channel where it isn't.

## Repro

Feed `buildProvidersConfigFromSettings` (`extensions/authentication/src/migration/providersJson.ts`) a reader with `authentication.anthropic.baseUrl = "https://api.anthropic.com"`. It writes:

```json
{ "providers": { "anthropic": { "baseUrl": "https://api.anthropic.com" } } }
```

Chat requests against that config 404. In-app: set the setting globally, remove `~/.posit/ai/providers.json`, run the `Migrate Provider Settings to providers.json` command.

Exposure requires the migration to run before the assistant's on-disk settings rewrite (`fixBaseUrlSettings`) corrects the value. Today that's unlikely: automatic migration is disabled (`maybeAutoMigrate` is commented out), and the manual command runs long after the assistant's startup rewrite. But #15121 enables auto-migration at the authentication extension's activation, with no confirmation prompt — and both extensions activate on `onStartupFinished` with no ordering guarantee, so users upgrading from a build predating the assistant's rewrite can migrate the bare host before it's fixed, on their first startup. Worth fixing the mapping before or with #15121. Enforced/default values are unaffected (only explicitly-set global values migrate).

## Fix

Apply `normalizeBaseUrlForProvider` when mapping `baseUrl` values. Upcoming work converging the migration onto a shared settings translator in `ai-config` (follow-up to posit-dev/ai-lib#32 / #14710) fixes this structurally; filing separately so the bug is tracked independently of that schedule. Since #14928 hasn't shipped, fixing before the release avoids ever writing a broken providers.json.

title: Chat: Leaking vestigial AI right click menu options
description: With `"chat.disableAIFeatures": true,` ie VS Code: Chat disabled, there are still "vestigial" options for sending to Chat that don't work with Posit Assistant itself. These need to be addressed so it doesn't look like there is AI features enabled (ie disable = true) and we'd need to evaluate hooking them into Posit Assistant * Explain + Review are non-functional * Gutter ✨ is present and non-functional --- With `"chat.disableAIFeatures": true,` ie VS Code: Copilot Chat enabled: * add selection to Chat * Open inline chat Both of which are only viable if Copilot is signed-in

title: Data connections: Expose Snowflake data lineage as context to Assistant
description:
Requested by @chetan-posit 

## Context

Snowflake natively tracks data lineage i.e. how data flows between objects (upstream sources → downstream targets). 

Reference doc: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/ui-snowsight-lineage

What lineage covers:
* Two relationship types: data movement and object dependencies.
* Supported objects: all "table-like" objects — tables, dynamic tables, external tables, Iceberg tables, views, materialized views, semantic views — plus stages and ML objects (Datasets, Feature Views, Models).
* Column-level lineage between any two table-like objects (with a "distance" indicating hops).

## AC

1. We want to surface lineage as context to Assistant so it can answer questions like "where does this table's data come from?", "what breaks if I change this column?", and "is this derived from PII-tagged sources?".

2. Spike on best way to expose this information 
3. Implement or create followup tickets 


## What Snowflake provides
No dedicated REST endpoint. Programmatic access is via SQL, callable through the SQL API (POST /api/v2/statements), connector, or Snowpark:

- SNOWFLAKE.CORE.GET_LINEAGE (table function) — the primary interface. Near-real-time; returns upstream or downstream lineage for a given object, with a max traversal depth of 5. Snowflake notes it returns a subset of what the Snowsight Lineage tab shows.

```
SELECT * FROM TABLE(SNOWFLAKE.CORE.GET_LINEAGE(
    'MY_DB.MY_SCHEMA.MY_TABLE',  -- object name
    'TABLE',                      -- object domain: TABLE, COLUMN, STAGE, ...
    'DOWNSTREAM',                 -- or UPSTREAM
    3                             -- depth (max 5)
  ));
```

```
ACCOUNT_USAGE views (OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES, ACCESS_HISTORY) — bulk/graph-building alternative, but with 45min–3h refresh latency. Better for periodic sync into our own store; worse for interactive queries.
```

## How might we expose this
1. Extend the existing Snowflake skill - add a lineage section to the Snowflake SKILL.md in posit-dev/assistant with GET_LINEAGE query patterns, the object-domain/direction/depth parameters, and the gotchas. 
2. On-demand structured tool - a first-class get_lineage(object, direction, depth) tool alongside the schema-context tooling from #14658. 
3. Context injection on selection — when the user has an object focused in the Data Connections pane, prefetch 1–2 hops up/downstream and include a compact serialization in the Assistant's context, alongside the schema context 

## Notes 
1. Enterprise Edition (or higher) required for data lineage feature.
2. Lineage is not available for the following kinds of objects:
- Objects in a shared database.
- Objects in the shared SNOWFLAKE database.
- Objects in the INFORMATION_SCHEMA of a database.
- Semantic views created before early February 2026.

https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/ui-snowsight-lineage#limitations-and-considerations

title: Data Connections: Display Semantic Views for Snowflake
description: ## Context [Semantic views](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/views-semantic/overview) are used in Snowflake to store shared business logic used by both humans and agents. We need a way to programmatically list semantic semantic views in Snowflake. The Snowflake REST API's [View resource](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/reference/view) (GET /api/v2/databases/{database}/schemas/{schema}/views) does not return semantic views, it maps to SHOW VIEWS, and semantic views are a separate schema-level object type surfaced only by SHOW SEMANTIC VIEWS. There is currently no dedicated semantic view resource in the [Snowflake REST API reference](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowflake-rest-api/reference). The cortex analyst api endpoint only allows POST https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst/rest-api [Example semantic view](https://app.snowflake.com/duloftf/posit_software_pbc_dev/#/data/databases/LENDING_CLUB_CLONE/schemas/PUBLIC/semantic-view/DATABOT_TEST/semantic-view-details) ## Acceptance Criteria 1. Technical spike on best way to query the semantic view information 2. Implementation or create separate tickets to build out the user journey ## User journey 1. When I open up the data connections pane with a Snowflake connection, I should see semantic views in the tree. 2. There should be a different icon for semantic views 3. When clicking on the semantic view, I can see a preview of more detailed information about the semantic view ## Proposed workaround Engineering to determine best solution: We may want to use the SQL Statements endpoint (POST /api/v2/statements) to run the SQL commands that do know about semantic views https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/views-semantic/sql Examples: SHOW SEMANTIC VIEWS (real-time, scoped) ``` POST /api/v2/statements { "statement": "SHOW SEMANTIC VIEWS IN DATABASE MY_DB", "warehouse": "MY_WH" } ``` Show catalog views (account wide) ``` -- per-database, real-time SELECT * FROM MY_DB.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SEMANTIC_VIEWS; -- account-wide, but subject to ACCOUNT_USAGE latency (up to ~hours) SELECT * FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.SEMANTIC_VIEWS; ```

title: New Folder Flow: URI scheme mismatch can leave a new Python env without a console session (web/remote)
description:
### Summary On web/remote, creating a Python environment through the New Folder Flow can end with the right interpreter selected but no console session. `python.createEnvironmentAndRegister` looks its `workspaceFolder` back up from a URI string (introduced in #14890), and on remote the main thread and the extension host disagree on that folder's URI scheme, so the lookup misses, throws, and the new venv's runtime metadata never gets registered. ### Root cause (confirmed via local repro) #14890 changed the call site in `positronNewFolderService.ts` from passing the `WorkspaceFolder` object to passing `workspaceFolder.uri.toString()`, so `rehydrateWorkspaceFolder()` in `createEnvApi.ts` now looks the folder back up with `getWorkspaceFolder(Uri.parse(uri))`. That URI is the workbench/main-thread representation. On remote/web it is `vscode-remote://localhost:9000/var/folders/.../new-uv_XXXX`, but the remote extension host represents the same folder as `file:///var/folders/.../new-uv_XXXX`. Same path, different scheme, so `getWorkspaceFolder` misses and throws `Workspace folder not found for URI: ...`. `positronNewFolderService._newFolderTasks()` catches that error, logs `[New folder startup] Error running extension tasks`, and force-completes the startup phase without recording the new venv's runtime metadata. Nothing then auto-starts a session, and the console stays empty. Desktop is unaffected: both sides are `file://`, so the exact-URI lookup matches. Instrumented log line from the repro (3/3): ``` rehydrate entry: wanted=vscode-remote://localhost:9000/.../new-uv_736628 direct=MISS folders=[file:///.../new-uv_736628] -> resolved: UNDEFINED ``` ### Why it is not a registration race The first fix attempt (#15159's original commit) waited on `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` for the folder to "register." That cannot work: `openFolder(..., { forceReuseWindow: true })` restarts the extension host with the folder already present as `workspaceFolders[0]`, so it is never *added* and the event never fires for it. The folder is present the whole time, just under a different scheme, so the wait can only ever time out and re-throw. ### Fix `rehydrateWorkspaceFolder()` falls back to a path-based match against the extension host's own `getWorkspaceFolders()` when the exact-URI lookup misses (PR #15159). Still a #14890 regression. ### Evidence - e2e `New Folder Flow: Python Project > New env: uv environment` (`test/e2e/tests/new-folder-flow/new-folder-flow-python.test.ts`, `@:web`): 2 CI failures on ubuntu/chromium within ~14h of #14890 merging (2026-07-24). - Symptom: the status bar shows the new interpreter as Active, the Console shows "There is no session running.", and the test hangs at the `>>>` prompt until its 120s timeout. - Local repro confirms the scheme mismatch and that the path-based fix passes 5/5. ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence (updated 2026-07-27, supersedes earlier registration-race diagnosis) -- main-thread vs. extension-host URI scheme mismatch on remote/web, confirmed by local repro. - **Test:** [New Folder Flow: Python Project > New env: uv environment](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=New%20Folder%20Flow%3A%20Python%20Project%20%3E%20New%20env%3A%20uv%20environment%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fnew-folder-flow%2Fnew-folder-flow-python.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** the console never reaches the `>>>` prompt; the test waits out its 120s timeout in `waitForReady`. - **Signal:** Instrumented repro (3/3): `rehydrate entry: wanted=vscode-remote://localhost:9000/.../new-uv_XXXX direct=MISS folders=[file:///.../new-uv_XXXX] -> resolved: UNDEFINED`. The folder is registered the whole time, under `file://`, while the caller sent `vscode-remote://` -- same path, different scheme, so the exact-URI `getWorkspaceFolder` lookup misses and throws. The earlier registration-race reading was wrong: `openFolder({forceReuseWindow:true})` restarts the ext host with the folder already present as `workspaceFolders[0]`, so `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` never fires for it. - **Frequency:** 2/442 CI runs (0.5%), ubuntu/chromium; web-only (desktop matches on `file://`). - **Fix:** PR #15159 -- path-based fallback match in `rehydrateWorkspaceFolder()`. Verified: RED (await-fix) 3/3 fail, GREEN (path-fix) 5/5 pass locally, plus a unit test for the scheme-mismatch case. - **Hypothesis:** product regression from #14890 -- the URI-string round-trip it introduced does not survive the main-thread/ext-host scheme difference on remote/web.
